discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moire materials

nominees.name: Long Ju
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, USA

motivation: For more than four decades, fractionally charged anyons were thought to require strong magnetic fields and Landau levels. Theory predicted that topological flat bands could host fractional Chern insulators with no external field, but this long remained a theoretical idea. In 2023-2024, Xiaodong Xu's group in twisted MoTe2, Kin Fai Mak's group (with Jie Shan) through thermodynamic and optical probes of the same system, and Long Ju's group in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN observed the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect: quantized fractional Hall conductance at zero magnetic field, arising from spontaneous time-reversal breaking and band topology alone. These experiments turned an abstract prediction linking Chern numbers, band geometry and strong correlations into a real, tunable class of materials. They opened a rapidly growing field that includes zero-field anyons, possible non-Abelian states, and new routes to topological quantum computation.
